The revised fee structure is broadly based on !:>oU\ OM No. J-12011./6/2025-

to time by the Department of Legal Affairs, Ministry of Law & Justice,
Government of India.

IV.
Payment to CC,SCs/counsel appearing on behalf of the Union of India shall not
ordinarily be borne by EPFO unless specifically directed by the Central
Government .
v. 
The fee for written opinion/advice in Table B (Item 13) shall also be applicable
for legal opinion/advice pertaining to all other courts/tribunals and for
opinion/advice on any other matter, as well as for vetting of departmental
documents such as MoUs, agreements and legal notices etc.

VI.
A claim for fee for attending court hearing shall be entertained only if the
appearance of the panel advocate engaged, whether as conducting counsel or
arguing counsel, is recorded in the Daily Order Sheet relating to that hearing.
In any case where an advocate claims to have participated in a hearing but
his/her name does not find mention in the related Daily Order Sheet, the burden
of proving such participation shall lie on the panel advocate concerned.

a#idavit/rejoinder/caveat/miscellaneous application etc. shall be entertained
only when a copy of the filed document is enclosed with the bill.
VIII.
Ciaim for typing and photocopying charges shali be restricted to the number of
pages in the petition/counter affidavit/rejoinder/miscellaneous application etc.
IX.
A bill in respect of an individual legal case may be raised by a panel advocate
through LIMBS for each item of work, as listed in the Tables above, as soon as
it becomes due, without waiting for the legal case to conclude. The EPFO office
concerned shall process such bills promptly and payment shall be released
within one month of receipt of the bill complete in aN respects.
X.
The expression “Central Board’ or “EPFO” includes its offices and officers and
shall be construed according to the context.
XI .
“Identical cases” shall have the meaning assigned in the Ministry of Law &
Justice OM dated 24.09.1999, namely:
“Two or more cases where substantially identical questions of law or
facts are involved and where the main difference is in the names,
addresses of the parties concerned, amount of money involved, etc.,
where common or identical judgments are delivered irrespective of the
fact whether all the cases are heard together or not.”

XII .
Effective Hearing
(a) A hearing in which either one or both parties are heard by the Court shall
be treated as an efective hearing. However, if the case is merely mentioned
and adjourned, or only directions are issued, or only judgrnent is delivered,
it shall be treated as a non-effective hearing.
(b) in a civil case, a date on which plaint/petition/written statement is filed,
issues are framed, witnesses are examined by affidavit or otherwise, cross-
examination takes place, an important miscellaneous application is argued,
or final arguments take place, shaH be treated as an effective hearing.
(c) in a criminal case, a date on which charge or notice, as the case may be,
is framed against the accused, or testimony of witnesses including cross-
examination is recorded, or statement of the accused under section 281 or
313 Cr. P.C (now section 316 or 351 of BNSS, 2023) is recorded, or defence
witnesses are examined, or arguments on any important miscellaneous
application are heard, shall be treated as an effective hearing.
(d) A panel advocate to whom a case has been assigned shall attend all
hearings in that case, whether effective or non-effective.
(e) Classification of a hearing as e#ective or non-effective shall be determined
by the concerned sanctioning officer on examination of the judicial
order/Daily Order Sheet. No claim shall be admitted merely on the basis of
the description furnished in the bill.
XIII.
The competent authority for approval of legal fee bills shall be as per the
Schedule of Financial and Administrative Powers issued by EPFO, as
amended from time to time. It has also been clarified by Head Office Finance
vide note dated 01.09.2016 that the words “in each case” refer to recurring
expenditure. Accordingly, the power delegated under Item No. 22 may be
utilised by field offices for sanction of bill amounts.
XIV.
All professional fee bills, except bills unrelated to LIMBS court cases, shall be
raised by panel advocates through LIMBS only, along with the requisite
supporting documents. No bill shall be processed unless the relevant case
status and hearing details have first been updated in LIMBS.
XV.
Engagement of advocates from outside the panel shall be regulated in
accordance with the relevant provisions of the Legal Framework Document, as
amended from time to time.
xvi. 
Distribution of cases amongst panel advocates shall be fair and equitable and
shall be regulated in accordance with the relevant provisions of the Legal
Framework Document
8

<
xvii. 
Any issue on which this circular is silent, or in which any ambiguity remains,
shall be examined by the ACC (Zone) concerned. If the ACC (Zone) considers
that clarification is required, the matter may be referred to Head Office clearly
specifying the point on which clarification is sought.
xviii. 
All payments made to panel advocates shall be subjected to internal audit at
least once in each financial year.
12. 
The revised rates of fee shall be applicable from the date of issue of this
circular.
